title: Variant Threshold Enforcer: policy-driven canary and A/B safety layer
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a policy engine that enforces per-step thresholds and automated actions during model rollouts. The 'Variant Threshold Enforcer' (VTE) will be a compact evaluation/decision component used by the rollout controller to: 1) evaluate live telemetry and test-suite metrics against configured thresholds (latency p95, error rate, token-cost delta, hallucination/QA score regressions), 2) decide whether to advance the traffic step, pause, or auto-rollback, and 3) emit structured reasons and traces to the Console and audit logs. The engine must support: traffic splits for canary and A/B tests, shadow traffic mirroring, composite rules (e.g., if latency regresses AND error rate increases -> rollback), time-windowed evaluations, and soft alerts (warn but continue) vs hard guardrails (block). The feature should be pluggable so Dedicated and Private deployments can opt-in to VTE with policy config stored in the control plane.
acceptance_criteria: Rollout controller calls VTE after each step and receives one of: advance, pause, rollback, continue-with-warn
VTE evaluates at least these metrics: p95 latency, 99th latency, error rate, token-cost-delta, custom eval score delta (from quality monitor)
Policies can express composite conditions and time-windowed thresholds (e.g., 5m p95 > 200ms AND error_rate > 0.5%)
Console UI surfaces VTE decisions with icons, decision reasons, and metric snapshots for each step
Automated rollback triggers a documented incident/alert and creates an audit entry with payload and related PR/commit links
Unit + integration tests covering at least three rollback scenarios and one shadow-traffic validation pass
implementation_notes: Design VTE as a stateless policy evaluator that receives a compact telemetry payload and policy JSON. Policy DSL will be a small subset of boolean and numeric predicates with comparators, aggregation functions (avg, p95, rate), windows, and severity. Example policy expressiveness: {"name": "latency-sla", "expr": "p95(window=5m, model=my-model) > 250", "action": "rollback"} — actually stored as escaped JSON string in the control plane. We'll implement the evaluator in Rust (shared with runtime) for determinism and compile-to-WASM option for Private deployments. The rollout controller will call VTE synchronously after step-completion; fallback behavior if VTE is unavailable: proceed in degraded-check mode using a small local heuristics library (p95 & error rate).
design_decisions: 1) Use a small DSL instead of full policy engine to keep runtime overhead low. 2) Make policies hierarchical: global org-level defaults, project overrides, per-rollout ephemeral policies. 3) Store policy versions and require a human approval step for policy changes that are 'hard' guardrails. 4) Emit structured 'decision' objects to tracing and Console; display both metric snapshots and the exact rule that fired. 5) Implement simulator harness to run historical telemetry against candidate policies before enabling in production.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for DSL parser and predicate evaluator (edge conditions, NaNs, missing metrics)
- Integration test: synthetic workload generator that feeds telemetry to VTE + rollout controller to simulate step progression and rollback scenarios
- Shadow traffic validation: ensure mirrored requests don't affect production quota and that VTE can consider shadow-only metrics when configured
- Canary staging: deploy to dedicated test pool with a synthetic model and real metrics pipeline to validate Console visualization and audit logs
- Post-merge: run policy simulation on last 90 days of production metric slices to surface false-positive rules
